title: Nine in ten voters named corruption a major factor — 'corruption need not be illegal or even malicious to be extractive'
summary: Rubenstein sets two polling findings beside the book's definition of the word. Gallup finds more than 70% of Americans think corruption is widespread in business rather than only in government, and her argument to companies is not to wait for regulation before acting on it.
blockquote: Nine in ten voters called “corruption” a major factor in their vote (about the same as “cost of living”). Gallup recently found more than 70% of Americans believe corruption is widespread in business, not just in government. As the entrepreneur Eric Ries discusses in his (prescient!) book Incorruptible, "corruption" need not be illegal or even malicious to be extractive and obviously unfair.
